# sysutils_user (Data Source)

Looks up an existing user account by name or by uid. Exactly one of `name` and `uid` must be set; the other is filled in from the account that was found.

The lookup goes through the system's name service switch (NSS), like `id` or `getent passwd`, so it also finds accounts provided by directory services such as LDAP or SSSD, not only those in `/etc/passwd`. Unlike the [`sysutils_user`](../resources/user.md) resource, it does not require root privileges.

A missing account is an error. The data source is read during planning, so an account that a [`sysutils_user`](../resources/user.md) resource in the same configuration creates is only found if the data source depends on that resource, for example through a reference to its `uid` or with `depends_on`.

## Example Usage

### Look up a user by name

```terraform
data "sysutils_user" "www" {
  name = "www-data"
}

# Resolve the name of the user's primary group.
data "sysutils_group" "www" {
  gid = data.sysutils_user.www.gid
}

# Give a directory to the web server user, whatever its uid is on this host.
resource "sysutils_directory" "webroot" {
  path  = "/srv/www"
  owner = data.sysutils_user.www.name
  group = data.sysutils_group.www.name
  mode  = "0750"
}

output "www_home" {
  value = data.sysutils_user.www.home
}
```

### Look up a user by uid

```terraform
# Find out which account owns uid 1000, typically the first regular user.
data "sysutils_user" "first" {
  uid = 1000
}

output "first_user" {
  value = {
    name   = data.sysutils_user.first.name
    shell  = data.sysutils_user.first.shell
    groups = data.sysutils_user.first.groups
    # The GECOS field is usually "Full Name,Room,Work phone,Home phone".
    full_name = split(",", data.sysutils_user.first.comment)[0]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Username to look up. Conflicts with `uid`. When looking up by `uid`, the name of the account that was found.
- `uid` (Number) Numeric user ID to look up. Conflicts with `name`. When looking up by `name`, the uid of the account that was found. If several accounts share a uid, the first one in the user database is returned.

### Read-Only

- `comment` (String) The complete GECOS comment field, including any comma-separated parts after the full name (for example `"Alice Example,Room 42,,"`). An empty string if the field is empty.
- `gid` (Number) Numeric ID of the user's primary group.
- `groups` (Set of String) Names of the user's supplementary groups, that is every group the user is listed as a member of, except the primary group. Groups without a name are omitted.
- `home` (String) Home directory.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier (equal to `name`).
- `shell` (String) Login shell. An empty string if the passwd entry leaves it empty, which login programs treat as `/bin/sh`.

## Errors

| Situation | Diagnostic |
|-----------|------------|
| Both or neither of `name` and `uid` are set | `Invalid Attribute Combination` |
| No account with that name or uid exists | `User not found` |

## Caveats

- `groups` lists supplementary groups only. The primary group is available as `gid`; use the [`sysutils_group`](./group.md) data source with `gid` to get its name.
- `shell` and `comment` are read with `getent passwd`, which must be installed. It is part of glibc and of most other C libraries and BusyBox.
- The data source only works on Unix-like systems.
